source_title: Russia's international ice hockey ban overturned
source_excerpt:
Since the end of the Soviet Union in 1991, Russia have won the men's World Championship five times but have never claimed the women's title
Ukraine's ice hockey federation has expressed "deep outrage" at Russia being allowed to compete in international events again.
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) overturned the ban placed on Russia by the sport's global governing body, the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF).
Russia have been suspended from competing in IIHF events since the country invaded Ukraine in February 2022 and earlier this year the IIHF ruled they would remain excluded.
The Russian Ice Hockey Federation (RIHF) appealed that decision to Cas, which has upheld it following an in-person hearing at its headquarters in Lausanne, Switzerland.
In a statement, the Hockey Federation of Ukraine said it "respected the authority and status of Cas".
"At the same time, we express our deep outrage at this decision," it added.
It said the threats, which had formed the basis of the ban, had not disappeared, adding "against this background, the decision to allow Russian teams to international hockey competitions causes special outrage".
A statement from Cas , external said that arguments made by the IIHF "citing safety, security and other concerns" were "not supported by sufficient evidence".
Russia are now set to be part of IIHF events in the 2026-27 season, including the men's and women's world championships.
Ukraine's men have qualified for the top flight world championships for the first time in 20 years after winning promotion at this year's Division 1 tournament in Poland.
The IIHF would not confirm whose place Russia could potentially take but pointed to its statement which said: "The ruling also has significant practical implications for competitions already at an advanced stage of preparation.
"These decisions made by Cas do not consider the practical elements which cannot be implemented immediately."
Individual athletes from Russia were allowed to compete at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Italy under a neutral flag, although not in ice hockey.
The IIHF expressed "disappointment" , external with the ruling.
"The IIHF disagrees with this aspect of the ruling and maintains that its decisions were necessary to protect the safety and security of all participants and safeguard the integrity of its competitions," they said in a statement.
"While the IIHF respects the authority of Cas and will act in accordance with its ruling, the outcome does not remove the concerns that informed its assessments."
Germany will host the men's world championships in May and Frank Lutz, chairman of the German ice hockey federation, said: "We reject the return of Russian national teams to international ice hockey tournaments.
"Allowing Russia to participate entails significant security-related, political, and economic consequences for us as hosts. We are now evaluating the ruling together with the IIHF and will provide information regarding the next steps."
The United Kingdom, Finnish and Czech federations also condemned the decision to allow Russia to enter teams.
Jan Cerny, secretary general of Czech Ice Hockey said he "very unpleasantly surprised" by the decision adding: "The current stance of Czech ice hockey does not change with the CAS decision. We do not agree with Russia's participation in IIHF tournaments during the war of aggression in Ukraine."
The chairman of the Finnish Ice Hockey Federation, Heikki Hietanen, called the ruling "in it's entirety, incomprehensible".
Ice Hockey UK said: "While disappointed, we respect the authority of Cas, and will analyse the decision and its potential implications for Great Britain's national teams."
A statement from the RIHF said it "welcomes the decision" from Cas and stated it will work with the IIHF to "facilitate the return of Russian teams to competitions".

hi_body:
कोर्ट ऑफ आबिट्रेशन फॉर स्पोर्ट (Cas) ने रूसी आइस हॉकी महासंघ की अपील को स्वीकार करते हुए रूस पर लगे अंतरराष्ट्रीय प्रतियोगिताओं के प्रतिबंध को रद्द कर दिया है। खेल की वैश्विक संचालक संस्था, अंतरराष्ट्रीय आइस हॉकी महासंघ (IIHF), ने फरवरी 2022 में यूक्रेन पर आक्रमण के बाद से रूसी टीमों को प्रतिबंधित किया था।

Cas ने कहा कि सुरक्षा और संरक्षा चिंताओं के संबंध में IIHF द्वारा प्रस्तुत किए गए तर्क पर्याप्त सबूतों द्वारा समर्थित नहीं थे। परिणामस्वरुप, रूस के 2026-27 सीज़न के लिए पुरुष और महिला विश्व चैंपियनशिप सहित IIHF प्रतियोगिताओं में शामिल होने की उम्मीद है।

## प्रतिक्रियाएं और अंतरराष्ट्रीय रुख

इस फैसले पर अंतरराष्ट्रीय स्तर पर विभिन्न प्रतिक्रियाएं सामने आई हैं:

* **यूक्रेन:** यूक्रेन के हॉकी महासंघ ने इस निर्णय पर "गहरा आक्रोश" व्यक्त करते हुए कहा कि मूल सुरक्षा खतरे अभी भी बने हुए हैं।
* **IIHF:** संचालक संस्था ने निराशा व्यक्त की और कहा कि प्रतिभागियों की सुरक्षा और प्रतियोगिता की अखंडता के लिए उसके प्रतिबंध आवश्यक थे, हालांकि वह Cas के फैसले के अनुसार कार्रवाई करेगी।
* **राष्ट्रीय महासंघ:** जर्मनी, चेक गणराज्य, फिनलैंड और यूनाइटेड किंगडम के प्रतिनिधियों ने इस फैसले पर चिंता या विरोध जताया है। जर्मन महासंघ के अध्यक्ष फ्रैंक लुट्ज ने कहा कि रूस की वापसी से महत्वपूर्ण सुरक्षा, राजनीतिक और आर्थिक परिणाम जुड़े हैं।
* **रूस:** रूसी आइस हॉकी महासंघ ने इस फैसले का स्वागत किया और कहा कि वह अपनी टीमों की वापसी को सुविधाजनक बनाने के लिए IIHF के साथ काम करेगा।

## व्यावहारिक निहितार्थ और सत्यापन

IIHF ने उल्लेख किया कि इस फैसले के उन प्रतियोगिताओं के लिए महत्वपूर्ण व्यावहारिक निहितार्थ हैं जो तैयारी के उन्नत चरण में हैं, और Cas के निर्णय में उन व्यावहारिक तत्वों पर विचार नहीं किया गया जिन्हें तुरंत लागू नहीं किया जा सकता। IIHF ने अभी तक यह पुष्टि नहीं की है कि रूसी टीमें किस स्थान को ले सकती हैं।

पाठक अंतरराष्ट्रीय आइस हॉकी महासंघ (IIHF) और कोर्ट ऑफ आबिट्रेशन फॉर स्पोर्ट (Cas) के आधिकारिक पोर्टलों के माध्यम से आधिकारिक घोषणाओं और बयानों का सत्यापन कर सकते हैं।

en_body:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) has upheld an appeal by the Russian Ice Hockey Federation, overturning the suspension that barred Russia from international competitions. The global governing body, the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), had previously excluded Russian teams following the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. 

Cas stated that arguments presented by the IIHF regarding safety and security concerns lacked sufficient evidence. Consequently, Russia is expected to return to IIHF events, including the men's and women's world championships, for the 2026-27 season.

## Reactions and International Response

The ruling has triggered significant international reactions:

* **Ukraine:** The Hockey Federation of Ukraine expressed "deep outrage" at the decision, stating that the original safety threats remained.
* **IIHF:** The governing body expressed disappointment, maintaining that its exclusion decisions were necessary for participant safety and competition integrity, though it stated it will act in accordance with the ruling.
* **National Federations:** Representatives from Germany, the Czech Republic, Finland, and the United Kingdom voiced opposition or concern regarding the ruling. German federation chairman Frank Lutz noted that Russia's return entails significant security, political, and economic consequences.
* **Russia:** The Russian Ice Hockey Federation welcomed the decision and stated it will work alongside the IIHF to facilitate the return of its teams.

## Practical Implications and Verification

The IIHF noted that the ruling carries significant practical implications for competitions already in advanced stages of preparation, stating that Cas decisions did not account for practical elements that cannot be implemented immediately. The IIHF has not yet confirmed which specific spots Russian teams might take.

Readers can verify official tournament announcements and statements directly through the official portals of the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) and the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas).
en_title: Court of Arbitration for Sport Overturns Russia's International Ice Hockey Ban
